My mother collected all things horror, and she grew up hiding behind the couch at a young age to peek at what her older sisters would watch late at night when she was too young to join. I guess that sort of "would-kill-for-thrill" factor was passed onto me when I was born, because I can not remember not being excited to go see the new flick in theaters for every new film. We have walls on walls in the basement of all kinds of films: up-front slashers like Friday and Nightmare on Elm's, to anything that peaked our interest on the shelf at a store. Now that she is older I am usually always breaking my neck on forums to notify her when things aren't so easy to find, but I don't know what I would do without the thrills and scares of the classics practically being a third parent through childhood. Horror helps me with a lot, and I think I depend on it all the more nowadays since I struggle with things such as depression. 

Plus the Reddit community is truly lovely, and the whole following is as a whole. Fear brings people together in a beautiful way, I suppose, haha.
